Hi Alex / Priya \u0014

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Great discussion \u0014 summarizing the performance requirements and proposed next steps so we have a shared MAP (mutual action plan). I attached an editable SLO checklist (slo-checklist.xlsx) and included the recording. Please review and confirm accuracy.

Key ask from FintechCo (as discussed):
- Latency: P95 <= 300ms for single-request generation (goal: P95 <= 200ms for baseline flows).
- Throughput: sustain 100 qps steady-state, with spikes to 150 qps during peak windows.
- Concurrency: support 200 concurrent sessions (mostly short requests, avg token length ~40 tokens).
- Streaming: partial-token streaming required for chat UX \u0014 clients expect first-token within 300-500ms and continuous token streaming after that.
- Availability: canary rollout for production with a rollback target <= 5 minutes.

Open questions we flagged during the call:
1) Traffic profile: typical qps distribution over hour/day (you said spikes during 9\u201311am PT).
2) Payload characteristics: average prompt size, average response length, and % of streaming vs batch.
3) Canary/validation acceptance criteria for the rollout (metrics + decision owner).

Proposed immediate next steps (please confirm owners and dates):
- FintechCo: share a 48-hour traffic sample (CSV or link) and confirm streaming vs batch % (owner: Alex) \u2014 due 2028-03-17.
- Redwood: run an initial performance plan & target configuration and share recommended instance sizing + estimated cost (owner: Nikhil) \u2014 deliverable 2028-03-18.
- Joint: schedule a perf run (canary) for the week of 3/20 to validate latency/throughput (owner: Marissa to schedule).

If those timelines look right I\u2019ll lock in the perf-run time and share an agenda.

Thanks \u2014

Thanks Marissa \u2014 this looks accurate. Quick clarifications from our side:

- Traffic: our production tier for the pilot is about 80 qps baseline, with 150 qps peaks (as noted). We'll export a 48-72 hour sample from our API gateway and share by EOD Friday (3/17).
- Payloads: avg request prompt ~35 tokens, avg response ~55 tokens. About 70% of user sessions expect streaming (chat UI), 30% are single-shot batch calls.
- Streaming requirement: important that the UX sees first-token within ~400ms and subsequent tokens streamed. If that can't be met on our first pass we may accept a higher first-token latency for a short pilot, but will be a decision criteria for production.
- Canary: our SRE leads want canary run where we compare error rate and P95 against current baseline; acceptance if P95 <= 1.2x baseline and error rate < 0.5% over 30 minutes. Decision owner: Priya Shah (SRE).

We'll attach the traffic sample and a short doc with our consumer flows. Also, is there an expected cost ballpark for the 100 qps steady state? Even a rough monthly ops estimate will help us with internal approval.

Marissa / team \u2014 tagging in some technical notes and a proposed perf validation plan (high-level). Quoting Alex for context: \"avg request prompt ~35 tokens, avg response ~55 tokens, 70% streaming.\"

High-level approach we recommend for the initial validation run:
1) Baseline load test: simulate your 48-hour traffic sample for a 30\u201360 minute window focused on peak hour. Measure P50/P90/P95 and error rate.
2) Concurrency ramp: test up to 200 concurrent sessions that match your avg token lengths (40\u201360 tokens total). Watch tail latency and KV-cache warmup.
3) Streaming validation: run a streaming test using WebSocket/SSE clients to confirm first-byte latency (target <= 400ms) and sustainable token throughput. We will instrument to capture time-to-first-token and token emission rate.
4) Canary config: we will run the canary on a dedicated subset (10% traffic) with automatic rollback if error rate > 0.5% or P95 > 1.2x baseline for 15-minute rolling windows.

Instance sizing (initial recommendation):
- Pilot: 2x A100-equivalent GPUs with quantized FP16 serving profile, autoscale buffer +1 instance for spikes.
- Production (100 qps steady + 150 qps peaks): 4x A100-equivalent with batching tuned for your token distribution.

Estimated ballpark cost: pilot perf validation (one-time execution + short reserved window) \u2014 ~$2,500\u2013$4,000. Monthly infra for steady-state 100 qps (w/ 4x instances + autoscale buffer) \u2014 rough estimate $16k\u2013$28k depending on region and reserved capacity. We will provide a more precise cost sheet after reviewing the traffic sample.

Deliverables and owners:
- Redwood: perf-plan doc + test scripts (Nikhil) \u2014 target 2028-03-18.
- FintechCo: 48-72 hr traffic sample + baseline metrics (Alex) \u2014 target 2028-03-17.
- Redwood + FintechCo: schedule perf run for week of 3/20 (Marissa to coordinate).

I attached a short perf-plan checklist (I can share as a Drive link if preferred). If Priya wants to sit on the run we\u2019ll include her in the invite.

Thanks \u2014
